TESTED ON DATES WE CAN CHECK

How well does this baseline perform?

Every test issues a forecast using only earlier historical windows, then compares it with observed accumulation.

Rolling historical holdouts
Issue dateObserved gainPredicted gainAbsolute errorPrior anchor years

Tests run every 14 days and use only actual observations available through the analysis date. Both training and test windows must be complete. Overlapping windows and a small number of winters limit the strength of the evaluation.

WHAT GOES IN

Observed temperatures.
Transparent assumptions.

Hourly CIMIS air temperature powers the chill models. Daily minimum and maximum air temperatures power growing degree days.

Time convention

HOW IT WORKS

A baseline you can inspect.

The outlook averages complete matching calendar windows from at least two earlier years. The displayed spread is the 10th–90th percentile of those historical totals. It is not a calibrated confidence interval or a weather-service forecast.

Backtests report MAE, RMSE and bias, and compare the model with a baseline that carries forward the previous seven days’ average accumulation.

GDD uses max(0, (Tmin + Tmax) / 2 − base), with no upper cutoff. The 50°F default is a demo setting; choose the base for your crop/model.

Chill resets November 1 and ends February 28. GDD resets January 1. February 29 is excluded from chill to match the original project convention.

DATA QUALITY

Gaps stay visible.

Source QC codes M, Q, R, S, N, H and Y are excluded, along with impossible temperatures, inverted daily extrema, and isolated hourly spikes. Missing temperatures are not filled. Seasonal totals sum available increments; incomplete totals can be biased. The Dynamic Model holds state across missing hours.

The selection screen requires at least 80% valid winter-hourly and paired daily coverage. Only three stations have bundled weather; other orchard regions need an additional download through the Python collection module. Your inputs are calculated in your browser and are not sent to CIMIS.

A historical decision-support prototype. Check data coverage and crop thresholds before interpreting results.
